title: Space A Hub — C1: MCP Tool Contract
description: Tools exposed by the Space A MCP server to employee agents (Pillar 1 and any MCP client). v2 aligns with Pillar 3's Space/membership model: v1's single `team` claim could not express a person belonging to several Spaces, which broke the permission model at its foundation. Change policy: additive only from here. Adding optional fields or enum values is allowed; removing/renaming fields or changing their meaning is not. Consumers MUST ignore unknown fields.

transport.description: Every C1 call carries identity and trace metadata OUT OF BAND — in transport headers, not in tool arguments. MCP's own auth spec is not mature, so this is defined at the application layer. Identity is the precondition for the visibility model: without it, scoping cannot be computed at all.

Authorization.description: Issued by corporate SSO. The server resolves it to { user_id, agent_id, spaces[] }. NOTE: agent_id and spaces are derived from this token and are NOT accepted as request parameters — letting a client assert its own membership would void the whole permission model.

X-Space-A-Trace-Id.description: Correlates one problem-solving flow across agents. The originating caller generates it. If absent, the server issues one and returns it.

X-Space-A-Depth.description: How many agent hops deep this call is. Increment when acting on a Space A response by calling another agent. Server rejects depth > MAX_DEPTH (default 5) with rate_limited. This is a cooperative guard against runaway loops, not a defence against a malicious client; the hard backstop is the server-side token/call circuit breaker.

stdio.SPACE_A_TOKEN: Same token, passed as an environment variable at process launch (local development).

permissionModel.description: THE AGENT PATH MUST NOT BE A PERMISSION BYPASS. If a person cannot see something in the Pillar 3 UI, they must not be able to obtain it by asking their agent instead — otherwise the 'glass wall' guest view is meaningless. The MCP visibility rule is therefore identical to the UI's.
permissionModel.rule: An agent may read: (a) any Knowledge doc with visibility='org', PLUS (b) all data belonging to Spaces the caller is a member of. Nothing else.
permissionModel.enforcement: Server-side, derived from the token's spaces[] claim. Never from a request parameter.

visibility.description: Knowledge sharing scope, aligned with Pillar 3. 'org' = readable org-wide (the default: knowledge is meant to circulate). 'space' = readable only within the owning Space. NOTE: v1 used private|team|public; those values are gone.
visibility.x-migration: v1 public -> org; v1 team|private -> space

spaceId.description: e.g. 'sw-innov'. A Space is a team life (a floor in the Pillar 3 building metaphor).

context.description: Anchors for graph expansion. The richer this is, the fewer tokens the answer needs.

code.description: unauthorized = missing/expired token. forbidden = authenticated but outside the caller's Space membership. rate_limited = depth exceeded or circuit breaker tripped.

tools.name: search_knowledge
tools.description: Search the org's agent knowledge for a similar past issue and its solution. Call this BEFORE trying to reason a fix from scratch. Returns a condensed solution payload, not raw logs. Results are scoped by the permission model: org-visible knowledge plus your own Spaces.

query.description: The error message or problem statement. Raw text is fine.

space_id.description: Optional: restrict the search to one Space you belong to. Cannot be used to reach a Space you are not a member of — the server intersects this with your token's spaces[].

limit.description: Keep small. Every extra result is tokens spent.

space_id.description: The Space that authored this knowledge. May differ from yours — that is the point: knowledge crosses team boundaries.

tried_and_failed.description: Dead ends a previous agent already walked. Do not repeat them.

related.description: Graph-expanded neighbours. This is what a vector-only search cannot give you.

reuse_count.description: How many times this has been cited successfully. Higher = more trustworthy.

searched.description: Retrieval funnel. Proves the token saving: many candidates considered, few returned.

tools.name: open_issue
tools.description: Declare that you have hit a problem. Call this WHEN THE PROBLEM APPEARS, not after solving it. v1 deliberately had no such call; v2 adds it because Pillar 3's UI renders a live issue timeline (opened -> knowledge_linked -> resolved) and an in-progress issue simply cannot be drawn if nothing is recorded until the end. The orphan-record risk this creates is handled by server-side staleness sweeping, not by refusing to record.

space_id.description: Which Space this issue belongs to. Must be one you are a member of.

note.description: Human-readable one-liner for the timeline entry. Pillar 3 renders this verbatim.

tools.name: cite_knowledge
tools.description: Record that you found an existing knowledge doc relevant to an open issue. This is what produces a ReuseEvent — the single most important event in this system, because it is the moment one team's knowledge crosses into another's. Call it as soon as you decide to use a search result, not after the fix lands.

doc_id.description: The knowledge doc you are reusing, from search_knowledge results.

note.description: Why it applies. Rendered verbatim in the Pillar 3 timeline.

tools.name: resolve_issue
tools.description: Record the solution and close the issue. If the issue produced knowledge worth sharing, this is where it becomes a Knowledge doc.

tried_steps.description: What you tried that did NOT work. As valuable as the solution — it saves the next agent the same dead ends.

publish_knowledge.description: Whether to turn this solution into a reusable Knowledge doc. Default true — knowledge is meant to circulate.

note.description: Timeline entry text. Rendered verbatim by Pillar 3.

knowledge_status.description: 'merged' means the gatekeeper judged this a duplicate of existing knowledge and folded it in — the first line of defence against knowledge-base bloat.

tools.name: get_skill_candidates
tools.description: List repeated solution patterns that should be promoted into an automated Skill. A fix recorded 3+ times is a signal that a human should stop doing it by hand.
